from pagination import paginate


def test_page_two_size_two_returns_third_and_fourth():
    result = paginate(range(1, 8), 2, 2)
    assert result == [3, 4]
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_page_numbers_are_one_based():
    result = paginate(range(1, 8), 1, 2)
    assert result == [1, 2]
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_empty_input_returns_empty_list():
    result = paginate([], 1, 2)
    assert result == []
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_invalid_page_returns_empty_list():
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3], 0, 2) == []
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3], -1, 2) == []


def test_invalid_page_size_returns_empty_list():
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3], 1, 0) == []
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3], 1, -2) == []


def test_page_beyond_last_page_returns_empty_list():
    result = paginate(range(1, 8), 10, 2)
    assert result == []
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_last_partial_page_returns_remaining_items():
    result = paginate(range(1, 8), 4, 2)
    assert result == [7]
    assert isinstance(result, list)

patches.rationale: The paginate function uses zero-based slicing (start = page * page_size), so page 2 returns items[4:6] = [5,6] instead of [3,4]. The fix is to make page numbers one-based by computing start = (page - 1) * page_size. This preserves the existing guard for invalid inputs (page < 1 or page_size < 1 returns []), preserves empty input returning [], and naturally returns [] for pages beyond the last page since slicing an out-of-range start yields an empty list. The return type remains a list because slicing a range or list produces a list. A new regression test file is added covering all acceptance contracts with exact input expressions and result types.
